'''Zhou Guangzhao''' {{Post-nominals|list=[[Fellow of the Royal Society|ForMemRS]]}} ({{zh|s=周光召|p=Zhōu Guāngzhāo}}; May 15, 1929 – August 17, 2024) was a Chinese [[theoretical physicist]] who served as President of the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] from 1987 to 1997.<ref name="ChinaVitae_ZhouGuangzhao">{{cite web |url=http://www.chinavitae.com/biography/Zhou_Guangzhao/full |title=Zhou Guangzhao |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=<!--Not stated--> |website=China Vitae |publisher=Carnegie Endowment for International Peace |access-date=January 5, 2020 |archive-date=July 6, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190706011528/http://chinavitae.com/biography/Zhou_Guangzhao/full |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Zhou Guangzhao was born on May 15, 1929, in [[Changsha]], the capital of [[Hunan]] province. He was the 5th child of the civil engineer Zhou Fengjiu,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.qiushi.org/index.php?m=content&c=index&a=show&catid=116&id=34 |title=One of a Hundred Thousand: ZHOU Guangzhao-The Story of a Scientific Hero |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=<!--Not stated-->|website=In the Spotlight|publisher=Qiu Shi Science & Technology Foundation|access-date= January 5, 2020 |url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210306135919/http://www.qiushi.org/index.php?m=content&c=index&a=show&catid=116&id=34 |archive-date=2021-03-06}}</ref> and the younger brother of biochemist/geneticist [[Zhou Guangyu]]. He graduated from [[Tsinghua University]] in 1951, and then did graduate work in theoretical physics for three years at [[Beijing University]]. He stayed at Beijing Univ. on the faculty after completing his PhD. In 1957 he was sent to the [[USSR]] by the Chinese Atomic Energy Research Institute to work at the [[Dubna]] [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]].<ref name="ChinaVitae_ZhouGuangzhao"/>

==Professional career==
Zhou returned to China in 1960, where he worked on the [[China and weapons of mass destruction|Chinese nuclear weapons program]]. Zhou joined the Ninth Institute in May 1961 as the director of the theory group.<ref name=":36">{{Cite book |last=Zhang |first=Hui |title=The Untold Story of China's Nuclear Weapon Development and Testing: A Technical History |date=2025 |publisher=[[The MIT Press]] |isbn=978-0-262-05182-8 |series=[[Belfer Center]] Studies in International Security |location=Cambridge, Massachusetts}}</ref>{{Reference page|page=23}}

He ultimately becoming director of the Chinese Nuclear Weapons Research Institute, now the [[China Academy of Engineering Physics]] (CAEP). 

He was elected to the [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]] (CAS) and later became the Vice President (1984–1987) and President (1987–1997) of the CAS.

Zhou's theoretical work focuses on particle physics.

He first visited the US in 1979. In the 1980s he spent time as a visiting researcher at the University of California and [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute]] and at the [[European Organization for Nuclear Research]] in Switzerland.<ref name="ChinaVitae_ZhouGuangzhao" />

==Death==
Zhou died on August 17, 2024, at the age of 95.<ref>{{cite news |title="两弹一星功勋奖章"获得者周光召逝世，享年95岁 |url=https://www.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_28446515 |access-date=18 August 2024 |publisher=The Paper |date=18 August 2024}}</ref>

==Honors==
The [[asteroid]] [[3462 Zhouguangzhao]] is named after him.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://minorplanetcenter.net/db_search/show_object?object_id=3462 |title=(3462) Zhouguangzhao = 1950 TL2 = 1977 SQ2 = 1977 TL6 = 1981 UA10 |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=<!--Not stated-->|website=International Astronomical Union Minor Planet Center |publisher=The International Astronomical Union|access-date= January 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>Minor Planet Circ. 26424</ref>

Zhou was elected to the US [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 1987.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/guangzhao-zhou-w5gwfq/ |title=Zhou Guangzhao|author=<!--Not stated--> |date=<!--Not stated--> |website=Member Directory |publisher=National Academy of Sciences|access-date= January 5, 2020}}</ref>
